time.desc: Country Y Leaders threatened to impose additional tariffs on social media and asked neighboring countries to fulfill their cross-border water delivery obligations before a cutoff.

Country Y Leaders announced on social media that they planned to impose high proportions of punitive tariffs on third countries that continue to trade with sanctioned targets, triggering public opposition and wait-and-see from many parties.

Country Y renewed pressure on Regional Organization A with tariffs, prompting the other party to suspend progress on the previously reached trade agreement and triggering a public confrontation at the official level

Country Y leaders threaten to impose extremely high tariffs on imports if neighboring countries move forward with trade arrangements with Country X, and neighboring governments publicly clarify that the arrangements are not free trade negotiations

Country Y The highest judicial body ruled that the large-scale tariffs implemented by the President under emergency powers were ultra vires. Subsequently, the President announced that he would use other legal channels to implement new global tariffs within a limited period.

Country Y The trade authorities announced the launch of special investigations on "overcapacity" in many countries based on existing trade laws to find new legal support for subsequent tariff measures.

Country Y Leaders publicly lashed out at the top judiciary and vowed to continue taxing in alternative ways, the same day Country Y held talks with officials from neighboring countries over the prospects of existing regional trade deals

Country Y Issue administrative measures to set extremely high tariffs on imported patented brand drugs and support exemption/tax reduction conditions and transition period arrangements for local production and pricing agreements
Country Y Adjust national security metal tariff rules, grant exemptions or reductions to some derivative products with lower content, and simplify tax calculation methods

Country Y Leaders threatened to impose the highest level of additional tariffs on Country X citing security concerns. Country X publicly denied the accusation and opposed tying security concerns to trade penalties.

Country Y Advance the implementation of a large-scale historical tariff refund system after tariffs were ruled illegal, while continuing to maintain global tariff measures through alternative legal tools

The Country X Embassy in City C criticized Leader A for imposing a 25% tariff on third countries trading with Country D, saying that it will take all necessary measures to safeguard interests and oppose illegal unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction; according to Institution Y1 data, there are still more than 140 countries in the world trading with Country D, and Country X will be the largest buyer of Country D77 % of oil exports in 2024.

Country Y Trade Representative E1 criticized Region A on Institution Z1 for not implementing the trade deal and not reducing any tariffs, and later defended the deal on Media S saying it was not comprehensive; Country Y President of the Distilled Spirits Council Person C3 warned Country Y and Regional Organization A that retaliatory escalation of spirits tariffs on both sides would create significant uncertainty

Country Z The minister responsible for Country Y trade Person H1 responded to Country Y’s 100% tariff threat, saying that Country Z and Country X had only resolved a number of important trade issues and did not pursue a free trade agreement; the previous week, Country Z had signed a mutual tariff reduction agreement with Country X to exchange automobiles for agricultural products.

Leader A resumes calling Country Z Prime Minister N governor and threatens Country Z with additional tariffs over trade deal with Country Z Country X; Country Z Leader A1 travels with Industry Minister Person G1 to City A1 meets with Region P Governor M to discuss federal automotive strategy

Country Z The government revealed that it is forming an automobile working group. The specific restrictions on Country X manufacturing electric vehicles to enter Country Z will be announced in the next few weeks, and Region P will participate in relevant coordination.

Country Y Institution V1 Ruling Leader A The 20% additional tariff imposed on Country X goods under Law I (linked to the national emergency related to fentanyl trafficking and trade imbalance) is ultra vires and constitutes a major setback in the trade war Leader A; however, other Law Q implemented under Law E and Law A are still valid, Leader A Says new 10% global tariffs will be implemented within 150 days

Institution V1 The ruling determined that the taxing power based on Country Y Law J belongs to Institution J rather than the president, and the regulatory authority assigned does not include the imposition of new taxes; the tariffs found to be illegal include the tariffs imposed on Country X, Country W, Country Z goods in February on the grounds of the fentanyl crisis, and the 10% to 50% tariffs imposed on countries around the world in April on the grounds of trade deficits.

A few hours after the ruling was announced, Leader A immediately signed an announcement to impose a 10% temporary tariff on imported goods from all countries based on Law N Law O, and announced on social media the next day that the tax rate would be raised to 15%; Law O allowed the president to impose a maximum tariff of 15% within 150 days, and Institution J would need to intervene after the expiration of the period.

Citing that the temporary tariffs implemented by Law O have brought uncertainty to countries that have previously negotiated 10% tariff agreements with Country Y (including Country E and Country B), Institution B2 trade policy chief Person E3 said businesses are tired and frustrated by the changing policies; economists pointed out that Law O requires tariffs to be implemented in a non-discriminatory manner and that previous bilateral agreements may be difficult to maintain.

After the announcement of the tariff ruling, Index S initially rose, but then fell sharply under the influence of Leader A's statement to increase tariffs to 15%; Company I2 chief strategist Person G3 believes that the tariff issue has become a supporting role and the core of the market is still the AI ​​story, and predicts that Leader A is unlikely to further increase tariffs due to its focus on affordability policies before the mid-term elections.
